low_power_modes_summary.n_a_at_protocol_layer: DALI does not standardize a sleep / wake protocol — a control gear must be ready to receive any forward frame at any time the bus is powered.
low_power_modes_summary.implementation_strategies: Implementing microcontrollers may sit in MSP430 LPM3 / LPM4 between forward frames, woken by the DALI_RX edge interrupt; Timer_A3 PWM may be gated when Actual Level = 0; TPS62260_ENABLE GPIO may be deasserted when the lamp is OFF; the WDT+ interval may continue to tick at ≈ 1 ms to count out the 15-minute Configuration Mode timeout.
low_power_modes_summary.no_explicit_sleep_command: There is no DALI command that places the gear into a low-power state. The protocol-defined power-related behaviours are: (a) Power On Level applied within 600 ms of bus power-up if no command is received; (b) System Failure Level applied on bus voltage loss; (c) information-memory update (TI_DALI_Flash_Update) triggered before VCC falls below 2.2 V (requires ≥ 3 ms VCC hold and ≥ 10.7 μF bus capacitance per § 5 footnote of SLAA422A).

fields.system_failure_level_behavior: On detection of a bus-voltage-loss event longer than the protected interval, the control gear shall set Actual Level := System Failure Level (Table 2 offset [1]).
fields.power_on_level_behavior: On bus power-up, the control gear shall set Actual Level := Power On Level (Table 2 offset [0]) within 600 ms if no DALI command arrives first.

flash_update_power_constraints.detection_method_TI: Comparator_A+ monitors VCC and triggers TI_DALI_Flash_Update before the brown-out threshold.

fields.notes: Any low-power behaviour beyond the System Failure Level / Power On Level pair is a property of the implementing silicon and firmware, not of the DALI protocol itself. Power-domain partitioning, isolation cells, retention, and UPF are concerns at the IP-integration layer and are out of scope for IEC 62386.
